newsitem.title: UK: More Shell staff hurt in Nigeria, Chevron reports trouble too.
newsitem.headline: More Shell staff hurt in Nigeria, Chevron reports trouble too.

text.p: Oil giant Shell said on Tuesday three more of its workers have been hurt in Nigeria, one seriously, and another oil company, Chevron, reported it too has been caught up in a local Nigerian political dispute.
Shell said more than 120 of its staff and contractors were still being held by the villagers who overran six oil flow stations in the western Niger Delta on Saturday.
"We regret to report that three more of the detainees were injured in a further incident last night...One is thought to be seriously hurt," said Shell spokesman Julian Barnes.

In Lagos, Chevron Nigeria, a subsidiary of the U.S.-based Chevron Corp, said that two of its oil installations in the oil-rich Nigeria delta were briefly picketed by villagers from two communities feuding with a local government over relocation of their headquarters.

"We had to shut down operations in the Utomana and Abiteye stations between 1500 GMT on Saturday and 1000 GMT on Sunday. All has however been normal since then in both stations with a combined production output of 8,000 barrels per day of crude," a company spokesman said. Shell said the community groups holding the staff and contractors in protest at the relocation of a local government headquarters had agreed to release all the injured staff but the company could not say when that would happen.
Some of the six workers hurt in Saturday's raid on the stations, which forced Shell to cut back oil production by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd), were released late on Monday, the spokesman said.
Oil exports and other supply commitments continued to be met, a Shell spokesman in London said.
Nigeria, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), produces 2.15 million barrels per day of crude of which Shell accounts for half.
The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Group's Shell said it planned a peaceful resolution to the feud between two villages in the oil-rich Delta.
